claims.text: The local catalog records the Lizardon / Charizard Mega Battle regional trophy source slice as spanning 1997-11-08/1998-04-26; the selected Pokumon snapshot separates the 1997-11-08/1998-02-15 qualifying window from the 1998-04-26 national event date.

Pokumon describes Lizardon Mega Battle, also called Charizard Mega Battle, as the second official Pokemon TCG tournament and says it was often billed as the first official national championships because the earlier official tournament was much smaller in scale.

The selected snapshot says qualifying tournaments were held across six locations in Japan from November 8, 1997 to February 15, 1998, and the live Pokumon article names those cups as Kobe Masara, Fukuoka Tokiwa, Tokyo Nibi, Osaka Hanada, Sapporo Sion, and Nagoya Kuchiba.

Pokumon says attendees were divided into junior and senior divisions, used single-elimination qualifier structures, and that top three players at each cup from each age division received No.1-3 Trainer cards while fourth-place players were invited onward without receiving a trophy card.

This child source slice models exactly three currently source-pinned PokéCardex UPC regional trophy rows: No.1 Trainer 021, No.2 Trainer 022, and No.3 Trainer 023. It does not model plaque variants, award-object copies, or a complete trophy object ledger.
The selected snapshot says the Lizardon regional No.1-3 Trainer cards were presented in acrylic plaques that designated the cup where they were awarded.

This source slice is the other side of the First Official Tournament confusion boundary: agents must not collapse Regional Lizardon Mega Battle 1997 No.1-3 Trainer rows into Pokemon Card Game Official Tournament 1997 No.1-3 Trainer rows, even though both families use No.1/No.2/No.3 trophy language.
The local source slice credits Mitsuhiro Arita for all three Regional Lizardon Mega Battle No.1-3 Trainer rows. This is source-scoped provider metadata, not direct physical-card authentication.

Local catalog examples show Arita's later footprint across major English-era cards, including Aquapolis-era work; this dossier uses that only as local artist-context texture, not a complete biography or proof of Japanese print facts.

Lizardon Mega Battle matters because it made early organized Pokemon feel national: regional cups named after real cities and Kanto towns, age divisions, a huge Makuhari Messe final, trophy cards, plaques, caps, and spectacle all turned play into ceremony. The cards are scarce objects, but the deeper collector reason is that they are fragments of the apparatus learning how to remember competition.

Agents should preserve Lizardon / Charizard Mega Battle context, regional qualifier lane, November 1997-February 1998 qualifier window, April 26 1998 final-event context, rank number, source row 021-023, Arita credit, plaque context, and First Official Tournament non-equivalence before accepting a match.

The cards are simple in the catalog -- No.1, No.2, No.3 -- but around them is a whole machine: city cups, age divisions, plaques, caps, a national stage, and Charizard as mascot energy. These trophy rows matter because they are not just rare; they are the apparatus leaving fingerprints of who was allowed onto the ladder.
